title: Slow-Roast Pork Belly with Crackling
subtitle: Pork belly roasted low and slow until the meat melts and the skin shatters
excerpt: Slow-roast pork belly is the most forgiving of roasts: the belly goes into a low oven for three hours and almost no attention is required. The fat renders slowly into the meat and keeps it tender. The skin blistered at high heat at the end becomes the crackling , crisp, salty, and completely irresistible.
sourceNotes: Roast pork with crackling is one of the most popular Sunday roasts in Britain. The belly cut, with its even layers of fat and meat, is particularly well suited to slow roasting and produces more reliable crackling than the loin because the skin is flatter.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Score the skin and season the pork the night before. Leave uncovered in the fridge overnight to dry the skin , this is the most important step for crackling.
recipe.temperatureNote: fan oven for slow roast, 220°C fan for crackling

glossaryTerms.definition: The pork rind that has been scored, dried, and roasted at high heat until it blisters and shatters. The key variables are a dry skin and sufficiently high final heat.

content.text: rests on two variables: a very dry skin and a very hot final blast of heat. The overnight fridge rest dries the rind completely. The slow roast renders the fat and cooks the meat without touching the skin with steam. The final 30 minutes at 220°C blisters the rind into crackling. Do not cover the pork at any point: steam is the enemy of crackling.

items.prepNote: skin on, in one piece, scored finely across the skin at 1 cm intervals

attrs.title: Score the skin deeply
attrs.body: Ask the butcher to score the skin, or use a very sharp knife or Stanley knife. The cuts need to go through the rind but not into the meat , about 2 to 3 mm deep. Fine, closely spaced scores produce more crackling surface area than wide cuts.

content.text: Mix the crushed garlic, rosemary, and fennel seeds if using with a little oil. Rub this mixture into the underside of the pork belly (the meat side, not the skin). Pat the skin very dry and rub generously with fine salt. Place skin-side up on a rack in a roasting tin. Refrigerate uncovered overnight or for at least 8 hours.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan. Remove the pork from the fridge and leave at room temperature for 30 minutes. Roast skin-side up for 2.5 hours. The skin should be pale and dry at this stage.
Increase the oven to 220°C fan. Roast for a further 25 to 30 minutes until the skin has blistered and crackled across its surface. Watch closely in the final 10 minutes.
Remove from the oven. Rest for 20 minutes before cutting. The crackling will soften slightly as it rests but will be crisp again within a couple of minutes.

items.symptom: The crackling is soft and chewy, not crisp
items.cause: The skin was not dry enough, or the final heat was not high enough.
items.fix: The overnight fridge rest is the most important step. The final temperature must reach 220°C fan. If the crackling is still soft, put it under the grill for 5 minutes , watch it carefully.

items.symptom: The crackling is hard and too dark
items.cause: The final temperature was too high for too long.
items.fix: Check the crackling at 20 minutes and every 5 minutes after. It should be golden-blistered, not charred. A slightly irregular colour is normal.

items.symptom: The meat is dry even after slow roasting
items.cause: Pork belly should not dry out , if it has, the oven temperature was too high.
items.fix: Keep the slow-roast phase at 160°C fan. The belly fat renders slowly at this temperature and keeps the meat moist throughout.

items.symptom: The crackling has not blistered across the whole surface
items.cause: Some areas of skin were thicker or had less scoring.
items.fix: Score the skin finely and evenly before cooking. After the slow roast, check that the skin is uniform in colour and texture before raising the temperature.

content.text: Roast pork with crackling is one of the foundational Sunday roasts of British cooking. The belly is the cut most often associated with it because the skin is flat and even, and the fat layers between the meat ensure the slow roast stays moist throughout. Serve with roast potatoes, apple sauce, and braised red cabbage. The crackling is the part everyone fights over.
